dataset_source.title: Sampling the materials space for conventional superconducting compounds
dataset_source.attribution: Source data: Tiago F. T. Cerqueira, Antonio Sanna and Miguel A. L. Marques, Sampling the materials space for conventional superconducting compounds, Materials Cloud 2023.163 v1, DOI 10.24435/materialscloud:qv-bq, CC BY 4.0. This catalogue is a derived projection with additional source-state screening commentary.

scope: Previously private source-model screening is now published as unscored source-computed material-design hypotheses. Historical private-screening wording is retained as context. These predictions are new to this reviewed catalogue only; experimental confirmation, worldwide first discovery, formal RPS and human scientific review are not claimed.
source_tc_scope: Source isotropic Eliashberg Tc in K at mu*=0.1 is a model result, not experimental Tc. It is a separate source product and is not associated with an individual Gaussian width or a numerical uncertainty interval.
pairing_response_scope: Retained ten-width lambda contrasts and independent source Tc products support bounded source-model comparisons. Chemical, mass, volume, sampling, spin and SOC effects can co-change; no universal causal or error-bound interpretation is assigned.
risk_tag_scope: Attention labels support browsing. Element labels are not measured magnetic ground states, rejection criteria or calibrated potential scores; no label does not mean no risk.

candidate.support_meaning: Preliminary screened support within the stated source model. This ordinal level is not a probability, formal RPS score or human scientific review.
candidate.risk_summary: Hydrogen desorption, zero-point/anharmonic response and decomposition compete with superconductivity. The exact source path is nonnegative and Gamma optical compression positive; force is zero by symmetry but fine pressure remains 0.288 GPa. The retained LaPtH3 control has larger lambda but lower separate Eli Tc, showing an omega/coupling tradeoff; AgPtH3 and LiPdH3 have still larger lambda with actual negative source paths, so they are not silently discarded or treated as stable superior cases.
candidate.ambient_scope: Both source SCFs converge, near-zero coarse forces/stress and bounded fine response are measured. Fine Fmax=0 eV/A, P=0.288 GPa, full max stress=0.288 GPa. Gamma optical compression is positive beyond printing bound and sampled path has no signed negative values. All listed q outputs have JOBDONE/last response convergence and no routine errors. This supports a finite-grid local/metastable source model, not global hull or experimental synthesis.
candidate.route_response: Li replaces Na on the alkali site with the Pt-H network and ordered sites retained. Source cell volume decreases 7.661%, changing the actual Pt-H/H-H distances. All ten lambda values and the independent Eli mu=.1 result improve versus NaPtH3. This is a coupled cation/bond-network construction, not an inferred mobile-carrier density or volume-only mechanism.
candidate.next_action: Use the frozen Li/Na roles to compare at common volume and common sampling, retaining lambda and omega separately, then address H loss or anharmonicity. Stable positive paired response supports the stated source domain; desorption/decomposition or disappearance under common method reverses it.

seven_criteria.identity: Complete ordered CIF/literal coarse-fine input/Gamma periodic species-site association is numerically supported; source input geometry and full tensor/forces are retained. Export occupancy is a discrete computational convention; source experimental P/T/occupancy and actual compiled unit constant are unknown. Exact-version input defaults scope the configured neutral scalar spin1/noSOC model, not magnetic ground state.
seven_criteria.quantitative_route_response: Li replaces Na on the alkali site with the Pt-H network and ordered sites retained. Source cell volume decreases 7.661%, changing the actual Pt-H/H-H distances. All ten lambda values and the independent Eli mu=.1 result improve versus NaPtH3. This is a coupled cation/bond-network construction, not an inferred mobile-carrier density or volume-only mechanism.
seven_criteria.pairing_relevance: Exact target and mapped control direct source lambda arrays have the same favorable sign at all ten common broadening tokens; omega_ln has explicit K units and separate Eli/McM mu=.1 tables remain independent. Same underlying q mesh is observed. The sensitivity range is not a physical error bound; sigma units, full-BZ convergence, experimental Tc and pure-geometry causality remain unknown. Literal method differences are declared confounds.
seven_criteria.ambient_feasibility: Both source SCFs converge, near-zero coarse forces/stress and bounded fine response are measured. Fine Fmax=0 eV/A, P=0.288 GPa, full max stress=0.288 GPa. Gamma optical compression is positive beyond printing bound and sampled path has no signed negative values. All listed q outputs have JOBDONE/last response convergence and no routine errors. This supports a finite-grid local/metastable source model, not global hull or experimental synthesis.
seven_criteria.competition_and_coherence: Hydrogen desorption, zero-point/anharmonic response and decomposition compete with superconductivity. The exact source path is nonnegative and Gamma optical compression positive; force is zero by symmetry but fine pressure remains 0.288 GPa. The retained LaPtH3 control has larger lambda but lower separate Eli Tc, showing an omega/coupling tradeoff; AgPtH3 and LiPdH3 have still larger lambda with actual negative source paths, so they are not silently discarded or treated as stable superior cases.
seven_criteria.novelty: Published DFT studies of LiPtH3/NaPtH3 hydrogen storage and metallic/mechanical/phonon properties are acknowledged. A 2026-10-07 exact-phase search found no experimental superconducting LiPtH3 benchmark. Novelty is the bounded matched Li-for-Na pairing-construction hypothesis in the reviewed catalogue, not first synthesis/composition.
seven_criteria.decision: Use the frozen Li/Na roles to compare at common volume and common sampling, retaining lambda and omega separately, then address H loss or anharmonicity. Stable positive paired response supports the stated source domain; desorption/decomposition or disappearance under common method reverses it.
